history.summary: A 1,206 sqft 3BR at Rivervale Crest (Sengkang, 99yr from Dec-1997, TOP 2002) asking $1.268M / $1,051 psf. It is the cheapest of three live 3BR asks in the project and sits at the 24-month same-size transacted median ($1,042 psf, 21 prints) — fairly priced, not a bargain. The algo's 848 is driven almost entirely by a -28.2% gap to the D19 age-adjusted median, but that gap is a stable Sengkang-vs-district sub-market level that has not converged in 24 years, not a unit-level dislocation; against the project's own deep cohort the ask is +0.9%. Deep liquidity and verified 3.7% yield make this an easy, honest asset to own — it just carries no forward edge.
history.rating_rationale: The one backtest-validated unit-level signal — cheap-vs-peers — does NOT fire once the correct comp set is used. URA prints for Rivervale Crest give 21 transactions in the tight size band (1,122-1,290 sqft) over 24 months at a median $1,042 psf, and 14 near-exact 1,206 sqft prints; the ask at $1,051 psf is +0.9% against that, i.e. market price. The most recent identical-size prints (Jan-26 $1.250M and $1.260M; May/Jun-26 $1.315M and $1.350M per realsmart) bracket the ask, so it is at worst fair and at best ~4% under the two newest prints — a rounding error, not an edge. The 848 rests on three channels that do not survive scrutiny: (1) age_value +17.6 from the -28.2% vs the D19 age-adjusted median ($1,465 psf) — D19 pools Serangoon/Hougang/Punggol stock, and deep-OCR LRT-only Sengkang has traded ~28% below that level persistently, so this is a location level already in the price, not mispricing; (2) appreciation +6.7 from the trailing 6.23%/yr CAGR, which per v3.5 priors has ~0 forward power and is visibly spent here — median psf went $745 (2021) -> $1,026 (2024) -> $1,067 (2025) -> $1,046 (2026, 14 sales), i.e. already rolling over, with momentum -1.0; (3) mrt +5.8 crediting 240m as MRT-grade when Rumbia SE2 is LRT-only. Netting out, forward expectation is roughly the OCR baseline (~3.7%/yr) less a lease-decay drag, plus 2.2% net carry — an ordinary outcome. Not an Avoid: unlike the project's 2BR (asked $1,111 psf against a $1,057 project average — genuinely above market, rated Avoid twice in June), nothing here is overpriced or artifactual. The very_low_psf flag is verified benign: $1,051 is simply this project's normal level on a 21-print cohort, with no sqft, format or bedroom mismatch. Fairly priced, liquid, no edge -> Neutral.
red_flags: Not cheap where it counts: +0.9% vs the project's own 24-month same-size cohort (21 prints, median $1,042 psf). The score_1000 of 848 comes from a -28.2% gap to the D19 age-adjusted median, which is a persistent Sengkang sub-market level, not a unit-level discount — do not credit it twice.

Lease is shorter than the DB record states: 99 years from 06/12/1997 leaves ~71 years today, not the 73 in the record (which back-derives from a 2003 built_year). At a 5-7yr exit the next buyer inherits ~64-66 years, where CPF pro-rating starts to bite — and realsmart shows this project's buyer base is 70% HDB upgraders, exactly the pool CPF rules constrain.

Price trend has already flattened: median psf $1,067 (2025) -> $1,046 (2026 YTD, 14 sales); factual_data momentum -1.0. The 2021-24 run (+38% on median psf) was the post-COVID OCR repricing and is spent.

LRT-only access (Rumbia SE2, ~194-240m; two stops to Sengkang MRT interchange). The MMR credits 240m as MRT-grade proximity (+5.8) — real daily convenience, but not an MRT premium, and it caps the tenant/buyer pool.

No seller scarcity: 21 same-size prints in 24 months, 50+ project deals in the past year, 490 units of which ~70% are 3BR, plus two competing live 3BR asks in the project. Exit will clear at the cohort median, never above it.
17.9% of matched resales here lost money (103 of 571) — the 82.1% profitable figure is deep and credible but not a floor; losses cluster in the 2013-2019 cohort.
Net yield 2.2% all-cash is thin carry, and per priors high yield predicts lower forward growth — it is income, never appreciation.
No dated catalyst: nearest future station is CRL Defu at 2.3km, which is not a Rivervale Crest catalyst; the future-infrastructure channel has no measured forward power regardless.

Floor and facing unknown — the listing states neither and there is no researched stack profile for this project. Same-size prints in the 06-10 band span $1.250M to $1.340M, so condition/renovation swings value more than floor here; a low-floor or unrenovated unit at this ask would be dearer than it looks.
ROI projections in this run compound the trailing 6.23% and show ~6.3%/yr — overstated. See appreciation_rate_override_pct.
catalysts: Cheapest live 3BR ask in the project: $1,051 psf vs $1,115 psf ($1.380M) and $1,163 psf ($1.390M) for the two other 3BR listings, and the bottom of the web-quoted $1,047-$1,163 psf live asking range. Entry discipline is the one genuine advantage here.

Exceptional liquidity and comp transparency: 1,059 lifetime transactions, 93 URA prints in 5 years, 34 in 24 months, 21 in the tight size band, 50+ deals in the past year. A clean, fast 5-7yr exit at a knowable price — rare at this quantum.

OCR region — the favoured forward region in the backtest (realized +3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1%, CCR +1.9%). This is a real signal, but it is the baseline available in any OCR asset, not a Rivervale Crest edge.

Deep buyer pool: $1.27M quantum sits squarely in the HDB-upgrader band, D19 buyer-pool depth scores very_deep, and buyer-pool depth is one of the few signals that survives clustering (std_beta +0.16).

Verified, artifact-free rental support: URA project-bed rent $3,900 vs realsmart median $3,825 over the latest 12 contracts (22 rentals last month, 3BR contracts $3,750-$4,000) — two independent sources agreeing on ~3.7% gross.

Amenity and family draw: Rivervale Mall at the doorstep (2-min walk), three primary schools within 600m (Rivervale 212m, North Spring 387m, Seng Kang 551m), full facilities incl. tennis courts and clubhouse. Supports the owner-occupier resale bid.

realsmart REALSCORE 3.8/5 with 82.1% of 571 matched resales profitable and 141 deals above 6% annualized — meaningful downside evidence on a deep sample that this project does not routinely lose owners money.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Solid and well-evidenced, unremarkable in level. Two independent sources agree: URA project-bed rent $3,900/mo and realsmart's median of the latest 12 contracts $3,825/mo (range $3,000-$4,700), with 22 contracts signed in the past month alone and recent 3BR leases clustering $3,750-$4,000. That gives ~3.7% gross / ~2.2% net all-cash — no yield artifact to verify, since the figure is nowhere near the ~5.5% suspect threshold. Demand drivers are genuine but mass-market: Rivervale Mall next door, three primary schools within 600m, two LRT stops to Sengkang MRT interchange. The tenant pool is families and HDB-decant demand rather than expat or CBD-commuter money, which caps rent growth at roughly inflation. Rental turnover is high and easy; rental upside is not a thesis.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Expect roughly the OCR baseline, less a lease drag — call it ~3.5%/yr, not the 6.23% trailing CAGR the run compounds. The trailing number is real but backward-looking and already spent: median psf ran $690 (2020) -> $745 (2021) -> $1,026 (2024) as the post-COVID OCR repricing worked through, then stalled at $1,067 (2025) and slipped to $1,046 (2026 YTD, 14 sales), with momentum -1.0. Per v3.5 priors trailing CAGR carries ~0 forward power, so it is story, not signal. The genuine forward positives are region (OCR +3.7%/yr realized) and buyer-pool depth; the genuine drag is lease, moving 71 -> ~65 years across a 5-7yr hold, which is the point where CPF pro-rating starts narrowing an already 70%-HDB-upgrader buyer pool. The -28.2% gap to the D19 age-adjusted median is not convergence fuel — Rivervale Crest has sat at that discount to newer, better-connected D19 stock for two decades and shows no mechanism to close it. Net: a market-rate entry into a market-rate asset, with the lease slowly working against the exit.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No researched profile exists for Rivervale Crest (stack_profile.status = not_researched), and the listing discloses neither floor nor facing — so stack quality is an open unknown, flagged rather than assumed. What the prints do show is that floor matters less here than condition: same-size 1,206 sqft units in the 06-10 band transacted anywhere from $1.250M (Sep-25, Jan-26) to $1.340M (Dec-25), a 7% spread inside one floor band, while the 11-15 band print (Jul-24, $1.250M) sat at the bottom of that same range. None of the artifact trust rules fire — no ask_above_own_stack_prints, no ask_below_stack_prints, no stack_low_floor_share >= 0.7, no bedroom_sqft_mismatch — so there is no PES/loft/ground-floor distortion behind this ask. The 3 baths on 1,206 sqft (402 sqft/bath) is generous for a 2002 Sengkang 3BR and worth confirming on viewing, but it does not create a two-tier PSF split here the way it did at Centro Residences: the tight-band cohort is a single, tight $1,005-$1,122 psf distribution. Practical read: at $1,268k the unit needs to be mid-floor and in reasonable condition to be fair value; if it turns out low-floor and unrenovated, it is dearer than the headline psf suggests.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: OCR realized forward baseline (+3.7%/yr, v3.5 28-district backtest) less a modest haircut for leasehold decay across the hold (71 -> ~65 yrs remaining, into the range where CPF pro-rating narrows a 70%-HDB-upgrader buyer pool). The trailing 6.23%/yr ura_5yr_cagr (93 txns) is deliberately REJECTED as a forward input: priors give it ~0 forward power, and the project's own annual medians show it is spent (median psf $1,067 in 2025 -> $1,046 in 2026 YTD, momentum -1.0). No override upward for the -28.2% district age-adjusted gap — that is a persistent sub-market level, not convergence fuel.

history.summary: A 1,668 sqft corner PENTHOUSE (top floor, ~7m double-volume ceiling, custom MCST/PE-approved loft deck) at Rivervale Crest, Sengkang, asking $1.88M / $1,127 psf on a 99yr lease from Dec-1997 (~70 years left, not the 73 in the record). The one URA print at exactly 1,668.42 sqft — Apr-2025, floor 16-20, the same penthouse format — went at $1,590,000 / $953 psf. The ask is +18.2% on that comp while the project's median PSF went the other way ($1,067 in 2025 -> $1,046 in 2026 YTD). $1.88M would also be the highest price ever recorded here in the 5-year URA book (max print $1,668,000). Same-size rental contracts say $4,000/mo, so the real gross yield is ~2.55%, not the 3.45% modelled. The 803 score is the district-gap artifact: -23.2% vs the D19 age-adjusted median is the permanent Sengkang sub-market level, while the project's own cohort prints the ask at a +7.1% PREMIUM.
history.rating_rationale: Priced above its own format's only comp, in a flat market, on the least liquid unit type in the project. The decisive comp is exact: 1,668.42 sqft, floor 16-20, Apr-2025, $1,590,000 ($953 psf) — the same top-floor penthouse format, 15 months ago. Asking $1.88M is +18.2% on that while Rivervale Crest's median PSF fell ~2% over the window, and it clears the project's 5-year record print ($1,668,000, Oct-24) by ~13%. Large units here trade at a PSF DISCOUNT, not a premium: the six ≥1,400 sqft prints since Jun-25 average ~$1,031 psf, which values 1,668 sqft at ~$1.72M, and the same-size penthouse print implies ~$1.59M. Fair range $1.62M-$1.78M; the ask is $100k-$290k over. The renovation cannot close it — the loft is a lightweight furniture deck on wood beams, usable space with zero strata area, so a valuer and a bank price 1,668 sqft and the buyer funds the gap in cash. Carry does not rescue it either: the 1,600-1,700 sqft band's own rental contracts are $4,250 (Jun-23) -> $4,000 (Jun-25) -> $4,000 (Jun-26), giving 2.55% gross / ~1.35% net on $1.88M, against the 3.45% the model assumed from a bedroom-adjusted project rent. Re-scored on honest inputs ($4,000 rent, 2.5%/yr OCR-baseline appreciation) the all-cash return is 2.26%/yr over 5 years and 2.50% over 7 — not compensation for an illiquid 70-year-lease asset. The score_1000 of 803 is the known failure mode: it is built on age_value +16.25 from a -23.2% gap to the D19 age-adjusted median, which is the persistent Sengkang location level that has never converged, while psf_premium_vs_ura_median_pct is +7.1% — cheap against the district, expensive against the project. The `very_low_psf` red flag is a size artifact (big unit, low PSF), not evidence of value. agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Weak, and materially worse than modelled. The run assumed $5,404/mo (rent_source ura_project, 39 contracts, bedroom-adjusted) for 3.45% gross / 1.83% net. The project's own contracts in the subject's 1,600-1,700 sqft band say otherwise: $4,250 (Jun-23), $4,000 (Jun-25), $4,000 (Jun-26 via realsmart) — three years of flat-to-down rent, all filed as 3BR. Sengkang tenants do not pay for square footage: 4BR-labelled units at 1,400-1,600 sqft rent $5,000-$5,500 while a 3BR at 1,600-1,700 sqft gets $4,000, so bedroom count drives rent and the extra 200 sqft of double-volume void earns nothing. At $4,000/mo on $1.88M gross yield is 2.55% and net ~1.35%, before the higher cooling and maintenance load a 7m-ceiling unit carries. Project-wide realsmart shows 3.7% est. yield on 22 rentals last month and a $3,825 median — that yield belongs to the $1.2-1.3M 3BRs, not to this quantum.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Do not use the 6.23%/yr trailing figure. It is the 2021-24 OCR repricing — median PSF $745 (2021) -> $846 (2022) -> $973 (2023) -> $1,026 (2024) -> $1,067 (2025) -> $1,046 (2026 YTD, 14 sales) — and it has already rolled over; factual_data momentum is -1.0. It is also drawn from a print book dominated by 900-1,300 sqft units (71 of 93 prints), so it carries the pooled size-mix risk this repo has flagged before. Forward, I use 2.5%/yr: the OCR baseline is 2.8% in config, and this unit sits below it because it has no unit-level discount to capture (it is at a premium to its own format), because the lease runs 70.4 -> ~63-65 years across the hold, and because the penthouse format is shedding rather than gaining buyer pool at Sengkang's price ceiling. On 2.5%/yr and $4,000 rent the all-cash return is 2.26%/yr over 5 years and 2.50% over 7 — versus the 5.94-6.00% the run projects by compounding the trailing rate. Backtest priors are explicit that trailing CAGR has ~zero forward power and that high yield does not predict growth; here even the yield leg is absent.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No researched profile for Rivervale Crest (stack_profile.status = not_researched), so the stack join is empty and floor/facing came from web research rather than the feed. What is established: this is a top-floor corner penthouse with ~7m ceilings, city views and a loft deck. That places it in the project's highest floor band, matching the Apr-2025 comp print at floor 16-20 — so the $1,590,000 / $953 psf comp is NOT a low-floor or PES artifact being compared against a high-floor subject. It is the same format on the same band, which is what makes the +18.2% ask gap decisive rather than suggestive. No low-floor trust flags fired (stack_low_floor_share 0.0, low_floor component 0.0). Worth noting for the file: the 1,668 sqft penthouses appear to be a small cluster (at least two have been marketed), not a one-off, so a future 1,668 sqft ask should be benchmarked against the $953-$1,012 psf band, not against the project's 3BR median. If this project is revisited seriously, run /research-development to map the penthouse stacks properly.
